# dsh-media-reader-0.1.0 — single-file edition
Everything below is the text of this bundle, in reading order. Binary payloads (lib/, python/,
fixtures/) are described in MANIFEST.json and are not inlined.


---

## README.md

```
# dsh-media-reader — install bundle

Give a DeepSeek Harness agent **eyes and ears**: read local images, audio and video — including on a model
route that cannot accept media at all — and turn a video into a **text evidence pack** (shots, frames,
music key/loudness/onsets, chords, transcripts) that any text-only model can work from.

Readable as plain text on purpose: a human can install it, and an LLM can read this file and act on it.

---

## What you are installing

| Piece | What it does |
|---|---|
| **plugin/** (`dsh-media-reader` <version>) | five tools — `media_probe`, `media_image`, `media_audio`, `media_video`, `media_evidence` — a `read_image` redirect for text-only routes, and a composer drop target |
| **skills/product-motion-studio** | the production method: brief → evidence map → storyboard → references → motion → deterministic assembly → acceptance gates. Without it the tools give you media access but no standards |
| **skills/dsh-plugin-install-safety** | why `dsh plugin add` must never be used here, and the copy-restore method plus the duplicate guard that prevents the split-Symbol crash |
| **skills/dsh-skill-install** | how to make a skill loadable and slash-invocable under `$DSH_HOME/skills` |
| **skills/dsh-test-boot** | boot a scratch instance BEFORE restarting the real server, and leave it up for the user to look at |
| **docs/** | the research, the production pipeline, the acceptance record, the evidence-pack format, the two direction workflows, and the reproducible film-pipeline commands |
| **fixtures/** | the small files the smoke test needs |
| **install.sh / install-skills.sh / uninstall.sh / smoke.sh** | everything, in four commands, reversible |
| **LICENSE** | the terms you are granted — proprietary, all rights reserved; personal non-commercial use only |

Requirements: **node**, **ffmpeg**, **python3** (with `faster-whisper` + `av` in a venv for local
transcription — see `docs/README.md`). No package manager is used and none is required.

---

## Install (5 minutes)

```bash
tar -xzf dsh-media-reader-<version>.tar.gz
cd dsh-media-reader-<version>

./install.sh --dry-run          # read every action first
./install.sh                    # copies the plugin into the profile, registers it, runs the guard
./install-skills.sh             # links the four skills into $DSH_HOME/skills
```

Then restart the DSH server so the tools register. Before you do that on a machine you care about, follow
`skills/dsh-test-boot/SKILL.md`: boot a second instance on a spare port, check it, and only then restart the
real one.

Verify for real (not just "it installed"):

```bash
DSH_TEST_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3096 ./smoke.sh
```

18 checks run against real sessions on **both** a vision route and a text-only route. The text-only checks
are the point: an image is returned as a factual description, the built-in `read_image` is redirected to
`media_image`, audio comes back as a transcript, and a video comes back as a described shot timeline with
the spoken transcript fused in.

Rollback: `./uninstall.sh` removes the copy and the patch row, and touches nothing else.

---

## The five tools

| Tool | Input | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `media_probe` | any media file | ffprobe facts: kind, duration, dimensions, fps, codecs, audio/subtitle tracks |
| `media_image` | PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF | vision route → the real image block; text-only route → a factual description from the configured vision route |
| `media_audio` | audio or video | local Whisper transcript with timestamps (`transcript.txt/.json/.srt`) |
| `media_video` | video | shot detection + bounded key frames + contact sheet + transcript fused to the shot timeline |
| `media_evidence` | video or audio | the full replication pack: tempo/key/loudness/timbre/regions/onsets, chord segments, shot boundaries with frames, lyrics confidence — every field tagged `MEASURED` / `INFERRED` / `UNVERIFIED` |

`media_evidence` is the important one: it is what lets a text-only model reason about a video it cannot
see. It is slow (1–4 minutes) and makes **no** generation call and no network request in the `local`
profile.

---

## Verification of this exact bundle

Built, installed and checked on 2026-11-03 from the tarball itself — not from the development tree:

```
./install.sh --home <clean-home> --profile web      # copy-restore, patch row, duplicate guard
./uninstall.sh --home <clean-home> --profile web    # removes only what it created
tar -xzf ... && ./install.sh (into the scratch profile) && ./smoke.sh
18/18 checks passed
```

All fifteen tool checks and the three drop-upload checks passed on the installed copy, on both a vision
route and a text-only route. `MANIFEST.json` lists every file with its sha256 so you can confirm what you
received.

## Adapt it to your own subject

Nothing in the pipeline names a subject. The portability contract is in `skills/product-motion-studio`:
one identity anchor per recurring subject, one scene per shot, motion in every shot, measured prices
rather than published ones, and every claim tagged with its evidence strength. A product film, a food
film, an architecture film and a music video follow the same pipeline; only the plates and the beats
change.

Provider ids, prices and limits **must be re-measured at run time** — `docs/PRODUCTION-PIPELINE.md` and
the skill both say so, because the published "from" price is the cheapest tier, not the tier you order.

---

## What this bundle deliberately does not do

- It never installs with a package manager (that is the crash vector this bundle exists to avoid).
- It never publishes anything, calls a generation provider, or spends credits.
- It does not claim to verify visual quality: acceptance is a separate, image-capable review, and the
  skill requires that verdict to be recorded next to the artifact.
- It does not include credentials. Any API key stays in the installer's own environment.

## Licence and provenance

**Proprietary — all rights reserved.** The full terms are in `LICENSE`, which ships in this bundle at both
the top level and beside the payload in `plugin/LICENSE`. In short: you may read, study, install and run
this for your own **personal, non-commercial** use; you may not copy, redistribute, resell or use it in a
commercial product without a written agreement. Commercial use is available on paid terms — open an issue at
<https://github.com/samorachumbi/dsh-media-reader/issues>.

Third-party components keep their own licences: `ffmpeg`, `faster-whisper` and the Whisper model weights
(downloaded at run time, **not** redistributed here), and the DeepSeek Harness packages. Those licences are
unaffected by the notice above.

Provenance: see `docs/ACCEPTANCE.md` for what was verified, on which date and harness version, and what
remains unverified. Model ids and prices in `docs/` are dated observations, not guarantees — re-check them.

```

## install.sh

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# dsh-media-reader installer — ANY DSH home, ANY profile, no package manager.
#
#   ./install.sh                      # auto-detect DSH_HOME (default ~/.dsh) and profile "web"
#   DSH_HOME=/opt/dsh ./install.sh    # explicit home
#   ./install.sh --profile scratch --home /path/to/home
#   ./install.sh --dry-run            # print every action, change nothing
#
# It is copy-restore on purpose: `dsh plugin add` forwards to pnpm inside the profile, which is the
# documented split-Symbol crash ("Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')" on every
# tool call). This script never invokes pnpm, npm, yarn or dsh.
set -euo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PKG_NAME="dsh-media-reader"
PROFILE="web"
DSH_HOME_DIR="${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}"
DRY_RUN=0

while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --home) DSH_HOME_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --profile) PROFILE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,12p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "install.sh: unknown option $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

run() { if [ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]; then printf '  would: %s\n' "$*"; else "$@"; fi; }

PROFILE_DIR="$DSH_HOME_DIR/profiles/$PROFILE"
DEST="$PROFILE_DIR/node_modules/$PKG_NAME"
PATCH="$PROFILE_DIR/cordis.patch.yml"
SRC="$HERE/plugin"

echo "dsh-media-reader installer"
echo "  home      $DSH_HOME_DIR"
echo "  profile   $PROFILE"
echo "  dest      $DEST"

[ -d "$HERE/plugin" ] || { echo "FATAL: plugin/ is missing from this bundle" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -d "$PROFILE_DIR" ] || { echo "FATAL: profile directory not found: $PROFILE_DIR (start DSH once with this home, or pass --profile)" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v node >/dev/null || { echo "FATAL: node is required on PATH" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null || echo "WARN: ffmpeg not found — media_probe/media_video/media_image need it"

# 1. copy (never a package manager)
run mkdir -p "$DEST"
for part in lib python package.json cordis.patch.yml README.md; do
  [ -e "$SRC/$part" ] || { echo "FATAL: plugin/$part missing" >&2; exit 1; }
  run cp -r "$SRC/$part" "$DEST"/
done

# 2. register the plugin row (idempotent)
if [ -f "$PATCH" ] && grep -q "$PKG_NAME" "$PATCH"; then
  echo "  patch row already present in $PATCH"
else
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]; then
    echo "  would: append the media-reader row to $PATCH"
  else
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$PATCH")"
    cat >> "$PATCH" <<'YAML'

# dsh-media-reader — images, audio, video and evidence packs on routes that cannot read media.
- insert:
    - id: media-reader
      name: 'dsh-media-reader'
YAML
    echo "  appended the media-reader row to $PATCH"
  fi
fi

# 3. duplicate guard — the crash vector this whole method exists to avoid
echo "  guard: materialised @deepseek-ai copies under profiles must be absent"
DUPES="$(find "$DSH_HOME_DIR/profiles" -type d -path '*/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/*' 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -n "$DUPES" ]; then
  printf 'FATAL: duplicate @deepseek-ai packages found — every tool call will crash until removed:\n%s\n' "$DUPES" >&2
  echo "  fix: rm -rf the paths above, then re-run this installer" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# 4. probe the plugin actually loads as a module.
#    On a real DSH home the host's own packages resolve through <home>/profiles/node_modules, so the
#    import works here. On a machine where DSH has not been started with this home yet, that tree does
#    not exist — that is a missing prerequisite, not a broken bundle, so warn instead of failing and say
#    what to do.
if [ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 0 ]; then
  IMPORT_ERR="$(node --input-type=module -e "await import('$DEST/lib/index.js')" 2>&1 || true)"
  if [ -z "$IMPORT_ERR" ]; then
    echo "  plugin imports cleanly"
  elif printf '%s' "$IMPORT_ERR" | grep -q "Cannot find package '@deepseek-ai/"; then
    echo "  WARN: the plugin cannot be imported from here because the harness packages are not reachable"
    echo "        from $DSH_HOME_DIR/profiles/node_modules. That tree is created by DSH itself: start the"
    echo "        server once with this home, then re-run this check. The copy and the patch row are in place."
  else
    printf 'FATAL: plugin import failed:\n%s\n' "$IMPORT_ERR" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi

cat <<NEXT

installed. Next steps:
  1. skills:  ./install-skills.sh          (links the bundled skills into \$DSH_HOME/skills)
  2. verify:  ./smoke.sh                   (needs a scratch instance; see INSTALL.md)
  3. restart the DSH server so the tools register, then run: dsh web --port <port>
  4. rollback: ./uninstall.sh --home $DSH_HOME_DIR --profile $PROFILE
NEXT

```


---

## install-skills.sh

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Link the bundled skills into $DSH_HOME/skills so they are loadable and slash-invocable.
# DSH reads $DSH_HOME/skills (NOT ~/.claude/skills) and hot-reloads changes.
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
DSH_HOME_DIR="${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}"
TARGET="$DSH_HOME_DIR/skills"

[ -d "$HERE/skills" ] || { echo "FATAL: skills/ missing from this bundle" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$TARGET"
echo "linking bundled skills into $TARGET"
for dir in "$HERE"/skills/*/; do
  name="$(basename "$dir")"
  [ -f "$dir/SKILL.md" ] || { echo "  skip $name (no SKILL.md)"; continue; }
  if [ -e "$TARGET/$name" ] && [ ! -L "$TARGET/$name" ]; then
    echo "  skip $name (a real directory is already installed there — not overwriting)"
    continue
  fi
  ln -sfn "$dir" "$TARGET/$name"
  echo "  linked $name"
done
echo "done. DSH hot-reloads this directory; no restart needed for skills."

```


---

## uninstall.sh

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Remove ONLY what install.sh created: the copied package and its patch row.
set -euo pipefail
PROFILE="web"; DSH_HOME_DIR="${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}"; DRY_RUN=0
while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --home) DSH_HOME_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --profile) PROFILE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    *) echo "uninstall.sh: unknown option $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
DEST="$DSH_HOME_DIR/profiles/$PROFILE/node_modules/dsh-media-reader"
PATCH="$DSH_HOME_DIR/profiles/$PROFILE/cordis.patch.yml"
run() { if [ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]; then echo "  would: $*"; else "$@"; fi; }
if [ -d "$DEST" ]; then run rm -rf "$DEST"; echo "  removed $DEST"; else echo "  not installed at $DEST"; fi
if [ -f "$PATCH" ] && grep -q "dsh-media-reader" "$PATCH"; then
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]; then
    echo "  would: strip the media-reader block from $PATCH"
  else
    cp "$PATCH" "$PATCH.bak.$(date +%s)"
    python3 - "$PATCH" <<'PY'
import re, sys
path = sys.argv[1]
text = open(path).read()
text = re.sub(r"\n# dsh-media-reader[^\n]*\n- insert:\n(?:    .*\n|\n)*?      name: 'dsh-media-reader'\n", "\n", text)
open(path, "w").write(text)
PY
    echo "  patch row removed (backup kept beside it)"
  fi
fi
echo "restart the DSH server to drop the tools."

```

## smoke.sh

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Live capability check: drives real DSH sessions on a scratch instance and asserts the plugin works on
# BOTH a vision route and a text-only route. Never touches a production server.
#
#   DSH_TEST_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3096 ./smoke.sh
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
[ -f "$HERE/plugin/probe/smoke.mjs" ] || { echo "FATAL: probe/smoke.mjs missing from the bundle" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v node >/dev/null || { echo "FATAL: node required" >&2; exit 1; }
DEFAULT_MODEL="${DSH_TEXT_MODEL:-deepseek-v4-flash}"
DEFAULT_VISION="${DSH_VISION_MODEL:-deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp}"
echo "smoke: ${DSH_TEST_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:3096}"
echo "  text-only route:  $DEFAULT_MODEL"
echo "  vision route:     $DEFAULT_VISION"
DSH_TEST_URL="${DSH_TEST_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:3096}" node "$HERE/plugin/probe/smoke.mjs"

```

# Acceptance record — 2026-10-30

**Object:** `dsh-media-reader` at the working tree on branch `feat/media-reader`
**Harness:** DSH `0.1.1-rc.2`, scratch home `$WORKSPACE/.dsh-test-home`,
port `3096`; two sessions driven through the real `session.prompt`/`session.history` API.
**Models:** `deepseek-official/deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp` (vision route) and
`deepseek-official/deepseek-v4-flash` (text-only route).
**STT:** local `faster-whisper 1.2.1` + `av 18.1.0`, `base`, int8, 4 threads.

> Every row below is a real DSH tool invocation on a real fixture, not a unit test.
> The unit suite (`npm test`, 38 tests) covers parsers, routing, locking and error shapes separately.

## Image

| # | Route | Input | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| I1 | vision | `fixtures/hello.png` | **PASS.** `media_image` returned a real image block; the model answered “HELLO MEDIA” from the pixels. |
| I2 | text-only | `fixtures/hello.png` | **PASS.** `media_image` returned `<type>image-description</type>` from `deepseek-official/deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp` with latency; text read “HELLO MEDIA”. |
| I3 | text-only | built-in `read_image` | **PASS as a redirect.** The pre-execute listener returned `Error: This model cannot consume image blocks … Call media_image …`. It is an error by design, not a fake success. |
| I4 | vision | missing file | **PASS.** `Error: NOT_FOUND: cannot read "…/missing.png": not found`. |
| I5 | vision | JPEG bytes named `.png` | **PASS.** `Error: IMAGE_TYPE_MISMATCH: … has an image extension but its bytes are a different format`. |
| I6 | vision | 4000×3000 PNG | **PASS.** Attachment store normalized to 2048×1536; envelope reported `(downscaled from 4000x3000 px)` and the image block was attached. |
| I7 | text-only, `visionFallback: off` | `hello.png` | **PASS.** `Error: VISION_FALLBACK_OFF: …` with no description and no vision call. |
| I8 | text-only, `autoRedirect: false` | `read_image` | **PASS (mutation).** The built-in refusal returned unchanged: `model "deepseek-v4-flash" does not declare image input`. This proves the redirect is what changes I3. |

## Audio

| # | Input | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | real speech `fixtures/jfk.wav` (11 s) | **PASS.** `base` transcript: “And so my fellow Americans ask not what your country can do for you, ask what you can do for your country.” RTF 0.98. |
| A2 | video `fixtures/talking.mp4` | **PASS.** `media_audio` extracted the audio track and returned the same speech; visuals untouched. |
| A3 | silence `fixtures/silence.wav` | **PASS.** “no speech detected in 3.0 s … non-speech audio … out of scope”. Not an empty string. |
| A4 | non-speech tone (`sample.mp4`) | **PASS.** Video digest reported “no speech detected in the audio track”. |
| A5 | video with no audio (`silent.mp4`) | **PASS.** `Error: NO_AUDIO_TRACK: … has no audio track`. |
| A6 | STT runtime absent (before install) | **PASS.** `Error: STT_DEPENDENCY_MISSING: local speech-to-text is not installed: missing Python module: faster_whisper`. |
| A7 | `jfk.wav` with `maxSeconds=3` | **PASS.** Only the first 3.0 s processed; output carried `<truncated>only the first 3.0 seconds were processed</truncated>`. |

## Video

| # | Route/input | Result |
|---|---|---|
| V1 | vision, `talking.mp4`, digest | **PASS.** One contact-sheet image block attached; timeline fused the local transcript. |
| V2 | text-only, `error-demo.mp4`, question “What error number is shown?” | **PASS.** Contact sheet + two frame descriptions produced “ERROR 42”; the assistant answered **42** with the second-shot caveat. |
| V3 | vision, same question | **PASS.** The model answered **ERROR 42** from the attached contact sheet (no auxiliary description). |
| V4 | speech + visual together | **PASS.** Timeline carried both `said:` (JFK speech) and `on screen:` (ERROR 42) lines. |
| V5 | silent video, digest | **PASS.** Frames present; `said:` said “this file has no audio track”; transcript note said so. |
| V6 | static video, no cuts | **PASS.** Uniform sampling explicitly labelled `uniform; no scene cuts were detected`; unit tests cover the fallback. |
| V7 | text-only, digest | **PASS.** No image blocks returned; `<visual>` contained the vision-route description. |
| V8 | 20-minute video, T4 caps | **NOT VERIFIED.** No 20-minute fixture was processed; the caps exist in code/config but were not exercised end-to-end. |
| V9 | scene cuts, `multishot.mp4` | **PASS.** `scdet` found 3 shots; frames mode attached contact sheet + 3 frames (4 image blocks). |
| V10 | text-only, `mode=frames` | **PASS.** `Error: FRAMES_NEED_VISION: … use mode=digest on this text-only route`. |

## Measured STT (same 7.30 s clip, cached model, int8, 4 threads)

| Model | Wall time | RTF | Peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base` | 8.40 s | 1.15× | 390 MB |
| `small` | 18.76 s | 2.57× | 791 MB |

`small` was initially measured at 251.79 s because the timer included its 480 MB download. That number
is **not** an RTF and is recorded here only to prevent it being reused as one. Default is `base`; `small`
is available for short clips where its slightly better handling of one hard word matters.

## Defects found during acceptance and fixed

1. **PyAV 19 removed `metadata_errors`**, which faster-whisper 1.2.1 still passes to `av.open`; every
   transcription failed. Pinned `av==18.1.0` in `python/requirements.txt`.
2. **A 700-token vision budget returned no text on a complex contact sheet** (reasoning consumed the
   cap). Raised `visionMaxTokens` to 2000; the same image then described correctly.
3. **ffprobe reported `fps: 25` for a still PNG**; still images now omit frame rate/frame count.
4. **An audio-only `.mp4` was labelled video by extension**; probe now reports `kind: audio` when ffprobe
   sees no video stream.
5. **HF Hub/onnxruntime logging polluted stdout**; the worker now emits a `MEDIA_READER_RESULT` marker and
   the bridge searches for it instead of parsing the whole stream.

## Drag-and-drop uploads

The composer client registers a **📎 Drop media** target and accepts drops anywhere in the composer.
The host route is `POST /media-reader/ingest` (loopback-only, client marker required, raw bytes).

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `hello.png` | **PASS.** `{ok:true, kind:"image"}` with the HELLO MEDIA description. |
| `jfk.wav` | **PASS.** `{ok:true, kind:"audio"}` with the JFK transcript. |
| `error-demo.mp4` | **PASS.** `{ok:true, kind:"video"}` with the timeline, JFK speech and ERROR 42 visual description. |
| missing `x-media-reader-client` | **PASS.** HTTP 403. |
| `notes.txt` | **PASS.** HTTP 415, `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA`. |
| upload temp cleanup | **PASS.** `artifacts/uploads` empty after processing. |
| client bundle served | **PASS.** `GET /plugins/dsh-media-reader/client.js` → 200 and scratch boot clean. |

**Not visually verified:** the drop target's rendered position was not screenshotted — the sandboxed
browser did not render the page (Chrome timed out). The host route, bundle serving and boot are verified;
the operator must confirm the drop interaction in the UI.

## Native attachment gate vs drag-and-drop

The operator reported that dropping an **MP4** produced DSH's native
“Only PNG, JPG, WebP, and GIF images are supported” message. That is the host's
attachment gate, so the drop was not reaching the plugin client.

The client now installs `dragover`/`drop`/`paste` listeners on `window` in the
**capture phase** and calls `preventDefault()` + `stopPropagation()` before the
native handler. It accepts image/audio/video extensions by filename or MIME type,
so MP4, MOV, MKV, WebM, MP3, WAV, M4A and the rest are routed to the upload host.
The host route was already verified with `error-demo.mp4`; the change is about
which handler sees the drop first.

**Still not visually verified:** the drop target and the new window handler were
not screenshotted; the sandboxed browser timed out. If a drop still produces the
native PNG/JPG message, check the URL (the live 3080 does **not** have the plugin
until install/restart) and confirm the client bundle is loaded.

## Stuck native drag mask

A second drop defect: DSH's native **“Drag images here to add them”** mask appeared on `dragenter` and
stayed up after drop, because our capture-phase `drop` stopped the native `drop`/`dragend` reset. Fixed by
intercepting `dragenter` in the capture phase too, and dispatching `window.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent('dragend'))`
on drop as a fallback. The plugin's own status now shows **Analyzing …** / **Added … to the draft**
instead of leaving the native mask.

Not visually verified end-to-end: the sandboxed browser still cannot render the page, so the operator must
confirm the mask disappears after a drop.

## Not verified

- Live-profile installation and a real server restart (the scratch instance is on port 3096).
- A 20-minute video, a large real screen recording, and the video duration cap (V8).
- A real handset/audio device, microphone input, or streaming (out of scope).
- The `small` model on a long file; only the 7.30 s clip was measured.
- Publication: no npm package, licence, screenshot, leak-scan or pre-flight for release.
- A real client-facing review of the two scratch browser tabs.

## Reproduce the scratch instance

```bash
cd $WORKSPACE
DSH_HOME=$PWD/.dsh-test-home dsh web --port 3096
# API: POST /api/session.create, then /api/session.prompt, then /api/session.history
```

The scratch home has its own profile and a symlinked `.credentials.yaml`; it never boots `~/.dsh`.

## Repeatable smoke harness

`probe/smoke.mjs` drives the same 15 acceptance checks through the live session API and passed
**18/18** against the scratch instance on port 3096 (session
`session-47b329d2-f9b1-4636-946d-be73707c49fb`). The final three checks drive the drag-and-drop host
route for image, audio and video uploads. It scopes every assertion to the turn it just ran;
its first version searched whole-session history and false-failed because it matched an earlier
vision-route image result. That was a harness bug, not a plugin bug — recorded here so the script is
not "simplified" back into the same mistake.

Run it with:

```bash
DSH_TEST_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3096 node probe/smoke.mjs
```

## docs/AUDIT.md

```
# Audit — findings, corrections, and the better path

**Date:** 2026-10-30 · **Mode:** investigation / design audit · **Decision:** **Option A accepted — three build-days**
**Status:** audit and revised pathway only; **no plugin code written**

## Object pinned

- Previous deliverables: git `a438faba50c75f463362f0408a35647a587019c4` (`RESEARCH.md`, `CONTRACT.md`, `PLAN.md`).
- Harness: DSH `0.1.1-rc.2`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` `0.1.1-rc.2`; paths below are relative to
  `$(npm root -g)/@deepseek-ai/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/`.
- Prior art: npm registry metadata and `dsh-video-lens-0.3.2.tgz`, fetched 2026-10-30.
- STT: `faster-whisper` PyPI metadata and official README, fetched 2026-10-30.
- Empirical media probes: local `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` 6.1.1, synthetic files in `/tmp/media-probe`, 2026-10-30.

## Questions this audit answered

1. Are the five headline findings true?
2. Can the proposed `read_image` fallback actually return a successful description?
3. Is a nested model call the best description mechanism, or is there a better route?
4. Is the tool surface and file handling minimal and safe?
5. Does the three-day plan measure the things most likely to fail?

## Verdict on the previous findings

| Previous claim | Audit verdict |
|---|---|
| DSH has no audio modality | **Confirmed.** `MODEL_MODALITIES = ["text","image"]`, `dsh-llm-deepseek/lib/index.js:1612`. |
| Text-only routes receive `[image omitted …]` | **Confirmed.** `dsh-llm/lib/index.js:592-594`, projection at `:1585`. |
| Four image gates key off `inputModalities` | **Confirmed.** Minor doc bug: the heading said “three” while the table listed four. |
| `llm/stream` cannot rewrite a request | **Confirmed.** `next` closes over the original options, `dsh-llm/lib/index.js:1640`. |
| A plugin can make an auxiliary model call | **Confirmed as precedent**, `dsh-session-title-llm/lib/index.js:195-228`; **inside a tool remains unprobed**. |
| No second API key is needed | **Qualified.** True only while a vision route is configured in DSH and the nested call works. Image bytes still go to that vision provider; that is data egress, not a free/local operation. |
| `tools/post-execute` can power the automatic fallback | **Corrected — not as a successful result.** See F1. |
| Video should always be described by an auxiliary vision call | **Improved.** On a vision route the current model should receive the frames directly; no auxiliary call. See F2. |
| Local `small` Whisper is the right default | **Unconfirmed.** Measure `base` **and** `small`; choose from measured speed/RAM/accuracy. See F4. |

## Findings

### F1 — Blocker in the old plan: post-execute cannot turn a failed `read_image` into a success

Evidence:

- Replacing `value` on a failed result is explicitly forbidden:
  `tools/post-execute cannot replace the value of a failed result` (`dsh-tools/lib/index.js:3380-3382`).
- Replacing `content` spreads the original result, preserving `isError: true` and `error`
  (`dsh-tools/lib/index.js:3390-3394`). The model would receive **an error whose text is a description**, not a successful read.
- Moving one seam earlier does not solve it: a synthetic successful result from `tools/execute` is normalized through the **owning tool's** output schema and renderer (`dsh-tools/lib/index.js:3436-3451`). For `read_image`, that means producing its declared `{path, image}` value, not arbitrary text.
- Shadowing `read_image` with our own registration is not a clean alternative: duplicate names fail within a layer (`dsh-tools/lib/index.js:2524`, registration at `:2762-2770`), and cross-layer shadowing would be load-order-dependent and hostile to future harness changes.

**Better path:** keep `read_image` native on vision routes. On text-only routes, use `tools/pre-execute` to **deny with a corrective redirect**:

> `This model cannot consume image blocks. Call media_image with the same file_path; it returns a text description with provenance.`

A deny is materialized as `Error: <reason>` (`dsh-tools/lib/index.js:3109-3125`), so the model can act on it. This is honest, cheap, uses a documented decision type, and does not hide the original failure class. The actual description happens in `media_image`, not inside an interceptor.

### F2 — Major improvement: make **all visual presentation** route-aware, not just `media_image`

The old plan still paid for auxiliary vision descriptions during ordinary video digests. Better:

- **Vision route:** extraction returns the contact sheet (and selected frames on demand) as real image blocks plus transcript/timeline text. The **current** model interprets the pixels on its next turn. Zero auxiliary model calls, and better reasoning because the user's actual model sees the evidence.
- **Text-only route:** the same artifacts go to the configured vision route through `ctx.llm.stream`; the tool returns text only, with provenance.
- **Audio:** identical on every route — timestamped text, no model call in the plugin.

This yields one simple rule:

> **Ingest once. Present according to the route. Never describe pixels the current model can already see.**

### F3 — Major safety improvement: resolve every input through `ctx.fs`, not raw paths

Use the same pattern as `read_image`: `ctx.fs.resolve` → `stat` → `readBytes` for images
(`dsh-tool-fs/lib/index.js:273-285`, `:1037-1045`). For `ffmpeg`, obtain the canonical OS path through
`ctx.fs.processPath(target)` (`dsh-fs/lib/types/index.d.ts:88-97`; local implementation
`dsh-fs-local/lib/index.js:713-715`).

Benefits: relative paths resolve against the session workspace; missing/non-regular files fail through the normal FS taxonomy; and subprocess arguments are absolute canonical paths, so a model-supplied basename beginning with `-` cannot become an ffmpeg option. Raw `node:fs` reads of arbitrary model-supplied paths are rejected as a design choice.

### F4 — The STT choice is still unmeasured; the official benchmark says not to assume

The official `faster-whisper` README reports, for **13 minutes** of audio with the **small** model on an **i7-12700K, 8 threads**: int8 beam 5 took **1m42s** and used **1477 MB RAM**. That is a different, much faster CPU than this i5-8265U with single-channel RAM, and it is not a prediction for this machine.

On this machine only **~2.4 GB** was available with Chrome running. Therefore:

- Probe **both `base` and `small`**, int8, on the same real 60-second speech clip.
- Record wall time, RTF, peak RSS, and a hand-checked word-accuracy sample.
- Choose the default from those measurements; do not pre-commit to `small`.
- Keep one media job at a time and make the duration cap part of the result, not a silent truncation.

Source: [faster-whisper README — Small model on CPU](https://github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper#small-model-on-cpu), fetched 2026-10-30.

### F5 — The ffmpeg approach is viable, including the empty-scene edge case

Empirical, local:

- `scdet=threshold=10,metadata=print` detected the two deliberate cuts in a 6-second three-shot video at **2s** and **4s**, scores **27.693** and **20.611**.
- On a static synthetic video, scene-based extraction produced **zero frames**. The uniform-sampling fallback is therefore mandatory, not optional.
- A tiled contact sheet was produced successfully (**960×180**, **62 KB**), within the image budgets.
- Audio extraction to **16 kHz mono PCM WAV** and a silent-audio fixture both succeeded.

This supports building our own thin ingestion layer rather than adopting an unvetted plugin for it.

### F6 — “No second key” must not become “no privacy cost”

When a text-only route needs a description, image/frame bytes are sent to the configured vision provider. That is the intended fallback, but it must be explicit in the README and controlled by config (`visionFallback: 'configured-route' | 'off'`). With `off`, the tool must say that a text-only route cannot read the image without a vision fallback; it must not quietly send anything.

Local STT remains the privacy-preserving default for audio. Cloud ASR is a separate decision and is not silently enabled by slow local measurements.

### F7 — The third build-day needs a date

The previous planner schedule gives media 2026-10-30/31 and trading 2026-11-01/02. Option A adds a third media day but does not itself resolve that collision. This audit does **not** move trading. Choose the third media day explicitly before scheduling implementation tasks.

## Alternatives considered and rejected

| Alternative | Why not the default |
|---|---|
| `post-execute` description replacement | Leaves `isError: true`; cannot replace a failed value (F1). |
| `tools/execute` synthetic success | Normalized through the owning tool's schema/renderer (F1). |
| Shadow `read_image` | Duplicate/load-order fragile; changes a first-party contract. |
| Reroute whole requests with `agent/request` | Payload has no messages; user attachments are refused earlier; switching models mid-session is intrusive. |
| Direct OpenAI-compatible HTTP as the primary describer | Duplicates credentials/retry/attachment handling. Keep only as the documented fallback if the nested-call probe fails. |
| Cloud audio/video-native model | Could cover non-speech audio, but adds keys, cost and media egress; optional later, not v1. |
| Local vision model | Not viable on this T4 machine's available RAM. |
| Adopt `dsh-video-lens` | Useful reference, but different credential/model design, text-only output, and still unvetted. Build the thin layer; do not install it. |

## Revised architecture

```
model-supplied path
        │
        ▼
ctx.fs.resolve → stat → processPath/readBytes
        │
        ▼
media_probe ──► kind, duration, tracks, dimensions
        │
        ├─ image ───────────────────────────────┐
        ├─ audio ─► ffmpeg ─► local Whisper ────┤
        └─ video ─► scdet/uniform frames + audio┤
                                                ▼
                                   durable artifacts + bounded text
                                                │
                              current route declares image?
                              ┌─────────────────┴─────────────────┐
                             YES                                NO
                              │                                 │
                  attach contact sheet/frames          configured vision route
                  + transcript/timeline text           via ctx.llm.stream
                  (no auxiliary model call)            → text-only result
                              └─────────────────┬─────────────────┘
                                                ▼
                         provenance: source, processor, timing, skipped content
```

## Decision

Proceed with **Option A**, using the revised `PLAN.md` (v2). The architecture is sound; the old automatic-fallback mechanism was not. The revised path is simpler, more honest, and cheaper on vision routes.

## Not verified

- No nested `ctx.llm.stream()` call has been executed from inside a tool.
- No Whisper model has been downloaded or benchmarked on this machine; no transcription accuracy is claimed.
- No real DSH tool call, model-route switch, plugin boot, or acceptance-matrix row has run.
- Prior-art packages were metadata/source scanned only; `/repo-vetting` was not completed and nothing was installed.
- No real user video/audio sample was processed; ffmpeg probes used synthetic files.
- The third build-day's date and the four product-scope defaults still need operator confirmation.

**Trail:** revised `PLAN.md` v2, corrected `CONTRACT.md`, and this audit are committed in the project repo; vault project card and journal updated.

```

## docs/CONTRACT.md

```
# DSH modality contract — pinned

**Pinned:** 2026-10-30 · **Against:** DSH `0.1.1-rc.2`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` `0.1.1-rc.2`
**Root:** `dsh/` = `$(npm root -g)/@deepseek-ai/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/`

Re-verify by re-reading these lines. If upstream moves, the diff between this file and the tree **is**
the finding.

## 1. Modalities

```js
// dsh-llm-deepseek/lib/index.js:1612
const MODEL_MODALITIES = ["text", "image"];
```

**No audio, video or file modality exists.** Audio and video can never reach a model through DSH; they
must be converted to text (and video additionally to images).

Catalog (`dsh-llm-deepseek/lib/index.js:1595-1608`):

| Model | `inputModalities` |
|---|---|
| `deepseek-v4-flash` | absent → schema default `["text"]` |
| `deepseek-v4-pro` | absent → schema default `["text"]` |
| `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp` | `["text","image"]`, `imagePixelBudget: 640000`, `imageMaxBytes: 1048576` |

Configured default route (`~/.dsh/settings.yaml`): `deepseek-official / deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`.
Configured second provider: `k3` (Kimi) via `dsh-llm-pi-ai` — text-only, foreign route.

## 2. The failure we exist to fix

```js
// dsh-llm/lib/index.js:592-594
function textOnlyImageText(ref) {
  return `[image omitted because this model accepts text only; attachment sha256:${String(ref.attachmentId).slice(7, 15)}]`;
}
```

Applied in `adapterStream` (`dsh-llm/lib/index.js:1585`) whenever
`info.inputModalities !== undefined && !info.inputModalities.includes("image")` and any message carries
an image block (`projectImagesForTextModel`, `:685`). Note: `inputModalities === undefined` **passes**
this gate.

## 3. All four gates on image access

| Gate | Location | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| tool | `dsh-tool-fs/lib/index.js:941` | `read_image` throws `cannot read "…" as an image: model "…" does not declare image input; switch to an image-capable model to read images` |
| runtime projection | `dsh-llm/lib/index.js:1585` | image block replaced by the placeholder above |
| attachment admission | `dsh-host-apiproxy/lib/index.js:2755` | user-attached image on a text-only route → `attachment-error` / `MODEL_DOES_NOT_SUPPORT_IMAGES`, refused pre-session |
| adapter | `dsh-llm-deepseek/lib/index.js:1396` | `LlmError("… does not accept image input.", "UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT")` |

## 4. Image size limits

| Limit | Request (`dsh-llm-deepseek`) | Store (`dsh-attachment-local/lib/index.js:833-838`) |
|---|---|---|
| bytes | 1 MiB (`:1167`) | 20 MiB |
| pixels | 640 000 (`:1163`) | 64 Mpx |
| per side | — | 8192 px |

## 5. Extension seams (typed, used by first-party packages)

| Seam | File:line | Can it replace what the model sees? |
|---|---|---|
| `tools/post-execute` → `PostToolDecision{kind:'accept', content?}` | `dsh-tools/lib/types/index.d.ts:61`, `:431`; implementation `dsh-tools/lib/index.js:3360-3394` | can replace content, **but preserves `isError`/`error`**; replacing `value` on a failed result throws (`:3381`). Not a failure→success fallback |
| `tools/pre-execute` → `{allow,deny,ask}` | `:38`, `:418`; denial `dsh-tools/lib/index.js:3109-3125` | cannot supply a result, but `deny.reason` becomes model-visible `Error: …` — suitable for a corrective redirect |
| `tools/execute` | `:49`; normalization `dsh-tools/lib/index.js:3436-3451` | around-dispatch wrapper; a synthetic success is normalized through the **owning tool's** output schema/renderer, so it cannot turn `read_image` into arbitrary text |
| `agent/request` → `{provider, model, …}` | `dsh-agent-loop/lib/index.js:708` | route only, not messages |
| `agent/request-error` → `{kind:'retry'}` | `dsh-agent-loop/lib/index.js:653` | retry only |
| `agent/pre-step` → `{kind:'enter', messages}` | `dsh-agent/lib/types/runtime-types.d.ts:235` | injects messages before a step |
| `llm/stream` → `AsyncIterable<StreamChunk>` | `dsh-llm/lib/types/index.d.ts:43`, call site `:1640` | **NO** — `next` is bound to the original options; it is a stream transformer, not a request rewrite |

## 6. Service surface a plugin may use

| Service | Use | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `ctx.tools.register(defineTool({…}))` | tool registration | `dsh-tool-fs/lib/index.js:1005-1105` |
| `ctx.llm.stream(GenerateOptions)` | auxiliary model call (`purpose` must stay unset — closed union `'compaction' \| 'session-title'`) | `dsh-session-title-llm/lib/index.js:208-228`; `dsh-llm/lib/types/types.d.ts:367` |
| `ctx.llm.resolveModelInfo(provider, model)` | the route-capability check | `dsh-tool-fs/lib/index.js:925-943` |
| `ctx.attachments.saveImage({data, mediaType, name})` | mint an image block | `dsh-attachment/lib/types/index.d.ts:49` |
| `ctx.subprocess.spawn(spec)` | run `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` | `dsh-subprocess/lib/types/index.d.ts:91` |
| `ctx.fs.resolve` / `stat` / `readBytes` | safe input resolution and bounded image reads | `dsh-tool-fs/lib/index.js:273-285`, `:1037-1045` |
| `ctx.fs.processPath(target)` | canonical absolute path for ffmpeg argv; local backend returns `String(target.targetKey)` | `dsh-fs/lib/types/index.d.ts:88-97`; `dsh-fs-local/lib/index.js:713-715` |
| image block shape | `{type:'image', attachment: {attachmentId, mediaType, bytes, width, height}}` | `dsh-tool-fs/lib/index.js` `imageReadContent` |

## 7. Installation contract

`dsh plugin --profile <p> …` forwards to **pnpm** inside the profile (re-confirmed 2026-10-30: it printed
pnpm's own help). That is the known split-Symbol crash vector. **Install by copy-restore:**
`cp -r <plugin> ~/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules/<name>` + one `cordis.patch.yml` insert row.

## 8. Limits this plugin cannot cross

1. No audio modality → audio is always text.
2. No request-rewrite seam → automatic help must be a **redirect** on `tools/pre-execute`. A
   `post-execute` content replacement leaves the result failed, and a `tools/execute` synthetic success
   is normalized through the owning tool's schema. Neither can turn a failed `read_image` into a clean
   text success.
3. A **user-attached** image on a text-only route is refused before the plugin is ever reached.
4. Non-speech audio has no route through DSH at all.

## docs/EVIDENCE-PACK.md

```
# Evidence pack v1 — measure before you generate

**Status:** built and measured on this machine · **Date:** 2026-10-31 · **Generation calls:** none

This is stage 1 of `PRODUCTION-PIPELINE.md`. It reads a media file and writes a directory of
measurements — tempo, key, cadence, energy, timbre, regions, shots, frames, lyrics confidence, loudness,
hashes — where **every field carries its own evidence tag**, so nothing downstream can mistake a guess
for a measurement.

```
node bin/media-evidence.mjs "source.mp4" --mode replica --profile local
```

It needs no DSH server, no network and no API key, which is exactly what makes it testable before any
restart.

**In a chat session** it is also a tool — `media_evidence` — so the same measurement can be requested
without a terminal:

```
media_evidence(path="…/video.mp4", mode="replica", shots=20, lyrics=true)
```

The tool returns the claims grouped by evidence strength (MEASURED / INFERRED / NOT CLAIMED) and the paths
to the full pack. It is deliberately slow (about 1–4 min for a full-length music video) and is not
concurrency-safe: one measurement at a time on this machine.

## Why it exists

The Rick Ross test file proved the gap concretely: the plugin's `media_audio` capped transcription at
300 s of a 368.08 s file, Whisper was transcribing a *sung* vocal as if it were speech, and the video
half produced a contact sheet with no tempo, no key and no per-shot record. A generator fed that would
invent the missing half.

So this stage measures what can be measured locally, and **says so** where it cannot:

| The question | v1 answer |
|---|---|
| How fast is it? | measured, with candidates and an octave rival named |
| What key? | measured, with the correlation margin |
| What is the rhythm feel? | inter-onset intervals, accent per beat position, alternation, grid deviation |
| Where does the structure change? | measured novelty boundaries — never labelled "verse" |
| What instruments? | **not measured** — no separator, no classifier ran |
| What is on screen? | shot boundaries, start/mid/end frames, luma and palette; **not** camera, action, transition or text |
| What are the lyrics? | the transcript, plus Whisper's own confidence deciding speech-like vs sung-or-uncertain |

## What v2 adds (2026-10-31)

v1 measured the mix and the shots. v2 adds the four things a generator actually needs, and keeps the same
tagging rule:

| Stage | What it produces | Evidence tag |
|---|---|---|
| **Full shot inventory** | every detected boundary in `shots.json`, plus pilot clips chosen to satisfy the generation endpoints (3–8 s continuous) | MEASURED |
| **Chord candidates** | major/minor triads from the measured chroma, majority-filtered, with a confidence margin | **INFERRED** |
| **Stems** | Kie Suno `split_stem` separation, downloaded, then **each stem decoded and measured locally** | MEASURED (files + their own numbers) |
| **Semantic pass** | Kie Gemini 3 Pro conditioned on the measured facts: genre, vibe, instrument hypotheses, vocal delivery, structural roles, camera/action/transition/on-screen text for sampled shots | **INFERRED** |

Paid stages run **only** in the `assisted` or `cloud` profile:

```bash
node bin/media-evidence.mjs "source.mp4" --profile assisted --budget-credits 100
```

Every paid call is appended to `replication/<job>/kie-jobs.jsonl` with task id, model, media sent,
latency, credits before/after and the local files. The credential is `KIE_AI_API_KEY` from
`~/projects/Website_Builder/.env`; it is never printed (only a shape mask) and never written to the ledger.

New skipped-stage honesty: `local` now says **why** stems and the semantic pass did not run, instead of
leaving a reader to assume the model found nothing.

### Measured on the real source (assisted profile)

`RICK ROSS - HIGH DEFINITION (OFFICIAL VIDEO).mp4`, 368.078 s, one paid run:

| Result | Value | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| Shot inventory | **196 boundaries**, median 0.959 s, longest 85.5 s — 9 are long enough for a 3–8 s generation clip | MEASURED |
| Pilot clips | `#1 0–8 s`, `#6 37.913–45.913 s`, `#196 282.574–290.574 s` | MEASURED |
| Chords | 9 segments, all confidence ≥ 0.46, A minor dominant (agrees with the measured key) | INFERRED |
| Instruments | Synthesizer 0.90, Drum Machine 0.95, 808 Bass 0.95 | INFERRED |
| Vocal | "steady, deliberate, heavily punctuated", low register, gruff delivery | INFERRED |
| Structural roles | intro 0–48 s · verse 48–88 s · hook 88–252 s · bridge 252–280 s · outro 280–368 s | INFERRED |
| Per-shot descriptions | 6 sampled shots described (action, camera, on-screen text) — correctly mapped to **detected** shots 1, 8, 14, 21, 28, 35 | INFERRED |
| Stems | **refused by the provider** — see below | UNVERIFIED |

Cost of that run: **2.56 credits**, wall time 8 min 40 s (local measurement 4 min, paid stages ~4 min 40 s).
Credits are read before and after every call and written into `kie-jobs.jsonl`.

#### Report defects found by reading the rendered document (2026-10-31, fixed)

The operator read `REPLICATION.md` against `replication.json` and found three places where the document
disagreed with its own data:

1. **The shot table hardcoded `_UNVERIFIED_`** in the camera/action/transition column, so a pack whose JSON
   held real descriptions still rendered "unverified". The report now prints each graded value with its own
   tag, and a closing line says how many sampled shots carry an interpretation.
2. **The OCR note lied in one case**: it said "no semantic pass read this frame" even when the pass had been
   shown the frame and simply returned no text. Three situations are now distinguished — read-and-found-
   nothing, not-among-the-sent-frames, and no-pass-ran.
3. **A model answer containing a newline broke the table** (on-screen text came back as two lines). Table
   cells are folded to one line.

Also corrected from the same review: pilot clips were chosen as the **three longest shots**, which on a
music video means the title card, the spoken intro and the end card. They are now chosen from the measured
**highest-energy region**, spread across it, and a single-shot video is told to use its keyframe with
image-to-video instead of a clip.

#### Measured on a second source (copyright-free, 776.5 s)

`Copyright Free Epic Music - Journey To The Stars (Savfk)`, 1280×720 @ 30 fps, one paid run, **2.76 credits**:

| Result | Value | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| Key / tempo | E major (correlation 0.638) / 100.3 BPM | MEASURED / INFERRED |
| Regions | 17 novelty regions | MEASURED |
| Chords | 22 segments; **14 of 22 fit E major's diatonic set** (0.636), with the major/minor-third caveat stated | INFERRED |
| Semantic | "cinematic orchestral", epic/majestic, Strings 0.95 · Brass 0.90 · Orchestral Percussion 0.95 · Piano 0.90 · Choir 0.90; wordless SATB choir, legato, heavy hall reverb | INFERRED |
| Video | **one continuous static shot** — piloted as a keyframe for image-to-video, not as a clip | MEASURED |
| On-screen text | "Journey To The Stars / SAVFK" read from the keyframe | INFERRED |
| Lyrics | no speech detected (instrumental) | UNVERIFIED |

#### Two presentation fixes from the second review round (2026-10-31)

1. **Single-shot videos no longer print a pilot window.** The note said "use the keyframe" while the table
   still offered a 0–8 s clip, i.e. advice and data disagreed. A single continuous shot now produces
   `mode: "keyframe"` with the frame timestamp and path, and the report prints one line instead of a table.
2. **Old packs can be re-rendered without re-measuring.** `--rerender <pack.json>` rebuilds
   `REPLICATION.md` from the pack's own JSON: no network, no credits. This is what lets a rendering
   improvement reach artifacts produced earlier — it re-presents, it does not re-grade, and it says so.

```bash
node bin/media-evidence.mjs --rerender replication/<job>/replication.json
```

#### The stem blocker, measured

Kie's Suno stem separation **refuses commercially released audio**:

```
GENERATE_AUDIO_FAILED: This audio matches an existing recording in our catalog.
```

That was verified for **both** `split_stem` and `separate_vocal`, and the failed task was **not charged**.
It also fires on a *copyright-free* track (the Savfk piece above was refused too), so the trigger is
"recognisable in their catalogue", not "copyrighted". **Kie stem separation is therefore not a usable route
for arbitrary music uploads**, and the pack reports stems as UNVERIFIED with the provider's own message.

Remaining options, in order of preference: separate the **generated** cover (not in their catalogue), a
vetted local separator (Demucs is still unmeasured on this machine), or a crude local mid/side split that
would be labelled as such.

#### One more provider limit, measured

The semantic pass uploads audio and asks the model to fetch it. An **18.6 MB** upload produced
`400 Failed to get the file information` — which reads like a credential or format failure and is really a
size problem. The pass now encodes a **64 kbps mono** copy (≤8 MB; a 776 s track lands at ~6 MB) and states
in the pack which audio the model actually heard.

## The three tags

- **MEASURED** — a number computed from the samples or the pixels.
- **INFERRED** — the measurement exists but is not decisive (narrow key margin, rival tempo octave).
- **UNVERIFIED** — the pack does not know, and states the reason and the route that could answer it.

The graders that assign these are pure functions in `lib/evidence/pack.js` with tests in
`tests/evidence.test.mjs`, so a threshold can be argued with rather than discovered by reading a
template string.

## What runs

| Stage | Implementation | Network |
|---|---|---|
| Source facts | `ffprobe`, `sha256sum`, one ffmpeg pass running `ebur128` + `silencedetect` | none |
| Audio measurement | `python/dsp_worker.py` (numpy only) | none |
| Shot sheet | `ffmpeg scdet` + frame extraction + 16×16 pixel statistics | none |
| Chord candidates | `lib/evidence/chords.js` (triad templates over the measured chroma) | none |
| Lyrics | local `faster-whisper` via `python/stt_worker.py` | model download only if uncached |
| Stems | Kie `ai-music-api/separate-vocals`, `split_stem` (≤20 MB upload) | **paid** |
| Semantic pass | Kie `gemini-3-pro` chat completions with audio + keyframes | **paid** |
| Pack + render | `lib/evidence/*` | none |
| Generation | **not in this stage** | — |

### The DSP worker is numpy-only on purpose

librosa would pull numba and llvmlite (~200 MB) onto a machine with ~2 GB of usable RAM. The worker
implements the textbook versions instead, and — more importantly — it is **verified against synthetic
signals whose answer is known before the measurement**:

```
$ .venv-stt/bin/python python/dsp_worker.py --self-test
PASS  moving average matches convolution — interior max |delta| = 8.882e-16
PASS  120 BPM click track — reported 120.11 BPM
PASS  120 BPM onset count — reported 19 onsets
PASS  96 BPM with off-beat eighths — reported 95.77 BPM
PASS  alternating accents are measured — alternation ratio 0.856
PASS  steady 440 Hz tone has no rhythm — 1 onsets, tempo None
PASS  C-E-G triad reads as C major — reported C major (r 0.8324, margin 0.0492)
PASS  silence claims nothing — silent=True tempo=None
PASS  truncation is reported — analysed 3.0s of 6.0s
=> 9 passed 0 failed
```

`tests/dsp.test.mjs` runs that self-test through `npm test`, so a Python change cannot land without it.

**Four defects this ground-truth discipline caught that reading the code did not:**

1. Log-compressed spectral flux reported **63 onsets for a steady 440 Hz sine** — window-phase leakage, not
   rhythm. Total-energy rise reports 1, and click tracks keep all their onsets.
2. A cumulative-sum moving average was **off by one frame** and dropped its last column, which moved the
   strongest flux from the attack to an edge artefact: 57 fake onsets.
3. Integer autocorrelation lags **quantised the period**, so a perfect 120 BPM metronome reported
   **60.1 BPM** (the half-tempo family happened to land on whole frames). Fixed by fractional-lag
   interpolation and by refining the period against the same objective that selected it.
4. Accents sampled from a **single frame** per beat gave a flat vector on real hip-hop; percussive *share*
   instead of percussive *energy* saturated at 1.0. Peak energy inside the beat window fixes both, and the
   alternation test proves it: 0.856 on an alternating grid vs 0.030 on a flat metronome.

## Artifacts

```
replication/<job>/
  source.json           # ffprobe + sha256 + loudness + silence windows
  audio-features.json   # the full DSP result, including the 2 Hz series
  frames/               # start / mid / end PNG per shot
  lyrics/               # transcript.txt / .json / .srt + lyrics.json with confidence
  reference/
    audio-mono-22050.wav  # the DSP input (reproducible)
    source-audio.flac     # lossless copy for the generator stage
  notes/skipped.json    # every stage that did not run, and why
  replication.json      # the tagged pack
  plan.json            # preserve / change / evaluation, derived mechanically
  REPLICATION.md       # the human-readable pack
```

`plan.json` deliberately has an **empty `change` list**: v1 does not invent a transformation. The operator
states what must change (for example "characters become anime-styled") and it is recorded there before any
generation call.

The `series` block (2 Hz energy, harmonic ratio, onset strength and 12-value chroma) exists so a generated
take can later be compared against this source numerically rather than by opinion.

## Measured on this machine

The real acceptance run, `RICK ROSS - HIGH DEFINITION (OFFICIAL VIDEO).mp4`, 27,226,722 bytes,
368.078 s, 1280×720 @ 23.976 fps, AAC 44.1 kHz stereo:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| wall time | 4 min 16 s (source 48.3 s, audio 22.8 s, shots 123.1 s, lyrics 61.6 s) |
| peak RSS (whole tree) | ~536 MB |
| DSP time | 6.5 s for 368 s of audio, 523 MB inside the worker |
| audio measured | 368.036 s — the whole track, `truncated: false` |
| shots | 196 detected, 30 sampled (3 frames each) |
| artifacts on disk | 100 MB (74 MB lossless reference audio, 26 MB frames) |

That is the point of the stage: 368 s measured instead of 300 s truncated.

The confidence path is two-sided, not just a warning label: the same code reports the rap vocal as
`sung-or-uncertain` at mean log-probability −0.52 (**INFERRED**) and the JFK speech fixture as
`speech-like` (**MEASURED**), so the tag discriminates rather than defaulting to caution.

## Limits

- **Tempo, key and rhythm cannot be measured with certainty** from audio alone. The pack reports
  confidence, rival candidates and the octave alternative instead of a single confident number, and grades
  weak readings INFERRED or UNVERIFIED.
- **Loudness onsets** are rises in total spectral energy: a quiet hi-hat over a constant bed may not
  register. The beat grid and onset rate are reported alongside so the under-count is visible.
- **Accents** are measured in the percussive band; a dense mix can flatten the pattern, which is why the
  spread is reported rather than a "backbeat" claim.
- **No OCR**: tesseract is not installed, so on-screen text is UNVERIFIED with that reason.
- **No stems, no MIDI**: Demucs and Basic Pitch are not installed. Instruments stay UNVERIFIED until a
  separator runs, or a native audio model interprets the mix in the `assisted` profile.
- **No semantic pass**: `local` makes no model call by definition.
- Nothing here is a legal opinion; the operator confirmed rights to the source for testing.

## Testing it

```bash
npm test                                                       # 52 unit tests incl. the DSP self-test
.venv-stt/bin/python python/dsp_worker.py --self-test           # DSP ground truth alone
node bin/media-evidence.mjs fixtures/error-demo.mp4 --out /tmp/ev --no-lyrics   # 9 s end-to-end
node bin/media-evidence.mjs "like.mp4" --mode transform --profile local        # mode changes the plan
```

## Next step

The Kie generation adapter is built in `lib/kie/generation.js` with the CLI in
`bin/kie-generate.mjs`. It is **disabled by default**, requires both explicit enablement and a
positive per-task cap plus a cumulative pilot budget, and has no batch mode.

One paid test-asset run now exists: a requested 60 s V6 music generation and a 15 s 9:16 Kling
prompt-only video, recorded under `generation/maasai-audio-test/` and `generation/maasai-video-test/`.
These are test assets, not an accepted replica or transformation; motion and cultural detail still
need operator review.

The next step is to review those assets, choose a non-catalogued source for the music replica pilot,
and then approve a video-reference or animate-replace pilot. No batch run until the assets and pilots
are reviewed against this pack.

**Observed provider limit:** Kie refuses Upload And Cover for a catalog-matched recording even when
the source is labelled copyright-free. The first paid NEFFEX pilot was refused in 20.7 s at **0
credits**; the failure is recorded in `generation/neffex-cover-pilot-1/kie-jobs.jsonl`. The adapter
does not retry catalog refusals or modify the source to bypass them.

```

## docs/PLAN.md

```
# Coding pathway v2 — `dsh-media-reader` (Video / Image / Voice)

**Date:** 2026-10-30 · **Status:** plan only — **no implementation started**
**Decision:** **Option A — three build-days, ~15 hours** · **Audit:** `AUDIT.md`
**Third-day date:** TBD — 2026-11-01/02 is currently allocated to trading; do not collide with it silently.

> v2 changes two load-bearing decisions from v1: the automatic `read_image` fallback becomes a
> **pre-execute redirect** (post-execute cannot turn a failure into a success), and **video presentation
> becomes route-aware** just like images. Read `AUDIT.md` F1/F2 before implementing anything.

---

## 1. Product contract

Any model on this harness can ask about a local image, audio recording, or video and receive an answer
grounded in that file. On a vision-capable route the model receives real pixels; on a text-only route it
receives text produced by the configured vision route. Audio is always transcribed locally to text.
Every result carries source, processor, timing, and skipped content. Missing capabilities raise; nothing
is mocked.

### Defaults for the still-open scope questions

These are v1 defaults, not silent expansions:

- **Files only:** local image/audio/video paths; no URLs or YouTube.
- **Recordings only:** no microphone, streaming, or real-time transcription.
- **Private enabler:** tools-only plugin, no client UI, no npm publication.
- **Audio stays local:** cloud ASR requires a fresh operator decision if local STT fails its measurement.
- **Vision fallback:** uses the configured DeepSeek vision route; a config switch can disable that egress.

## 2. Architecture (the better path)

```
path → ctx.fs.resolve/stat → processPath/readBytes → probe
                                      │
              ┌───────────────────────┼────────────────────────┐
              ▼                       ▼                        ▼
            image                   audio                     video
              │                       │                        │
              │                ffmpeg → 16 kHz mono       scdet + uniform fallback
              │                       │                        ├─ frames + contact sheet
              │                  local Whisper                 └─ audio → local Whisper
              │                       │                        │
              └───────────────────────┴────────────────────────┘
                                      │
                    current route resolved with resolveModelInfo
                                      │
                    ┌─────────────────┴──────────────────┐
                 declares image                       text-only
                    │                                    │
          attach image blocks + text          configured vision route via
          (no auxiliary model call)           ctx.llm.stream → text only
                    └─────────────────┬──────────────────┘
                                      ▼
                    bounded result + artifact paths + provenance
```

Services used: `tools`, `llm`, `attachments`, `fs`, `subprocess`. No raw model-supplied filesystem reads,
no second credentials by default, no network outside the configured model route.

## 3. Repository and configuration

```
lib/
  index.js        # register four tools + one pre-execute redirect
  route.js        # current route + configured vision route
  fs.js           # resolve/stat/processPath/readBytes helpers
  exec.js         # subprocess argv, timeout, cancellation, cleanup
  probe.js        # ffprobe metadata
  describe.js     # auxiliary vision call via ctx.llm.stream + BlockAssembler
  image.js        # image admission and route-aware presentation
  stt.js          # local faster-whisper worker bridge
  video.js        # scene detection, uniform fallback, frames, contact sheet, fusion
  redirect.js     # read_image → media_image guidance on text-only routes
probe/            # measurement scripts and fixtures, not shipped
tests/            # node:test from the first implementation task
artifacts/        # generated transcripts/frames/digests, git-ignored
```

Config (all have safe defaults):

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `artifactsDir` | project `artifacts/` | durable outputs |
| `visionProvider` / `visionModel` | `deepseek-official` / `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp` | auxiliary description route |
| `visionFallback` | `configured-route` | `off` disables image egress and fails explicitly on text-only routes |
| `autoRedirect` | `true` | redirect `read_image` on text-only routes |
| `whisperModel` | chosen by Probe A | `base` or `small`, never assumed |
| `whisperThreads` | `4` | measured against RAM/CPU pressure |
| `maxAudioSeconds` | `300` | truncation must be stated |
| `maxFrames` | `4` (hard cap `6` on T4) | visual budget |
| `maxVideoSeconds` | `600` | video processing cap |
| `ffmpegThreads` | `2` | leave CPU for the harness/browser |

---

## DAY 1 — measurements, walking skeleton, image path (~5 h)

### 1.1 Baseline and fixtures (0.75 h)

- Branch `feat/media-reader` from the audited commit.
- Record the audited contract corrections in `CONTRACT.md` (already done in v2 docs).
- Prepare fixtures: small PNG, mislabeled image, static video, three-shot video, narrated clip, silence,
  no-audio video. Synthetic ffmpeg fixtures are acceptable for pipeline tests; acceptance also needs one
  real speech sample and one real screen recording.

### 1.2 Blocking probes (1.25 h, run downloads/benchmarks in the background)

**Probe A — STT choice.** Install `faster-whisper==1.2.1` in the project venv. Run the same real 60-second
speech clip through **`base` and `small`**, int8, fixed thread count. Record wall time, RTF, peak RSS and a
hand-checked accuracy sample. Select the default from the table below, and write the actual numbers into
the project notes.

| Result | Decision |
|---|---|
| `small` fits RAM and RTF ≤ 1.5× | default `small` |
| `small` works but RTF 1.5–3× | default `small` only within a shorter duration cap; document |
| `small` too slow/heavy, `base` acceptable | default `base`; state the accuracy trade-off |
| neither acceptable | **stop**; local audio is not viable on this machine. Ask before any cloud ASR |

**Probe B — nested model call.** A scratch tool makes one `ctx.llm.stream()` call with a real image block
to the configured vision route from inside `execute`. Required: a valid text response, no deadlock, clean
cancellation. If it fails, **stop and re-plan the describer**; direct HTTP is a fallback with new config
and credential work, not a drop-in freebie.

**Probe C — before picture.** On `deepseek-v4-flash`, invoke built-in `read_image`; capture the exact
refusal. This is the negative control that Day 1's redirect changes.

### 1.3 Skeleton + `media_probe` (1.25 h)

Implement plugin registration, config, FS resolution, subprocess wrapper, structured errors, and
`media_probe(path)`. Unit tests begin here: missing file, directory instead of file, relative path,
unsupported input, ffprobe failure. No model calls.

### 1.4 `media_image` + redirect (1.75 h)

`media_image(path, question?)`:

1. Resolve through `ctx.fs`; validate regular file and supported media type.
2. Read bytes with the attachment byte cap; `saveImage` performs real format/dimension validation.
3. Current route declares image → return text envelope + image block. **No auxiliary call.**
4. Otherwise, if `visionFallback=configured-route` → describe through the vision route with a fixed
   anti-fabrication prompt; return text with provenance and latency.
5. Otherwise/failure → explicit error naming the missing capability.

Register the `tools/pre-execute` redirect for `read_image` on text-only routes:

> `This model cannot consume image blocks. Call media_image with the same file_path; it returns a text description with provenance.`

### Day 1 acceptance

| # | Route / input | Required result |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | vision route, real PNG | image block + envelope; logs show no auxiliary call |
| I2 | text-only, same PNG via `media_image` | factual description + processor/latency/source |
| I3 | text-only via `read_image` | error redirects to `media_image`; follow-up call succeeds |
| I4 | missing file | explicit FS error, no description |
| I5 | JPEG named `.png` | attachment mismatch error, no inference |
| I6 | oversized image | succeeds within documented limits or names the exact limit |
| I7 | `visionFallback=off`, text-only | explicit refusal; no network call |
| I8 | redirect disabled | original `read_image` refusal returns (mutation test) |

**Day 1 stop gate:** image path passes both routes; Probe A numbers recorded; Probe B verdict known.
Do not start audio on an unmeasured STT choice.

---

## DAY 2 — local audio and video ingestion (~5 h)

### 2.1 `media_audio` (2.5 h)

Parameters: `path`, `language=auto|en|sw`, `model=<measured default>`, `maxSeconds=300`.

Pipeline: FS/probe validation → reject absent audio track → extract at most `maxSeconds` to 16 kHz mono WAV
→ local faster-whisper with Silero VAD → write `transcript.txt`, `transcript.json`, `transcript.srt` →
return bounded segments plus artifact paths, duration, detected language, processor, RTF, and truncation.

Guardrails: one media job at a time; merged cancellation/timeout; temporary cleanup in `finally`; model
cache inside the project; explicit dependency errors; no audio bytes sent to a model.

| # | Input | Required result |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | clear speech | accurate transcript, timestamps checked against the clip |
| A2 | video with speech | audio track transcribed; no visual claims |
| A3 | silence | “no speech detected” with duration, not an empty success |
| A4 | music only | no words + non-speech limitation stated |
| A5 | no audio track | explicit “no audio track” |
| A6 | missing venv/model | dependency error naming the missing piece |
| A7 | input longer than cap | only capped portion processed; truncation stated |

### 2.2 Video ingestion (2.5 h)

Implement ffprobe metadata, `scdet` parsing, uniform midpoint fallback when no cuts are detected, one
representative frame per selected shot, frame scaling inside the 1 MiB / 640 000 px request budget,
contact-sheet generation, and reuse of `media_audio`. Write `frames/shot-NN.png`, `contact-sheet.png`,
`timeline.json`, and transcript artifacts.

Unit-test the `scdet` parser against captured output and prove the fallback with a static-video fixture.
Enforce frame, duration, subprocess and concurrency caps.

**Day 2 stop gate:** audio matrix passes; a three-shot sample yields timestamped frames + contact sheet +
transcript; a static sample yields uniformly sampled frames and says why. Presentation to the model is
Day 3, but the artifacts must already be real and inspectable.

---

## DAY 3 — route-aware video, full acceptance, packaging (~5 h)

### 3.1 `media_video` presentation (2 h)

Parameters: `path`, `question?`, `maxFrames=4`, `mode=digest|frames|transcript`.

- `transcript`: return the audio result only; no frame work.
- Vision route, `digest`/`frames`: attach the contact sheet (and selected frames for `frames`) as image
  blocks, plus timestamp/shot metadata and transcript text. The current model answers `question` from
  those pixels; **no auxiliary vision call**.
- Text-only route, `digest`: send the contact sheet to the configured vision route for one coarse visual
  digest; use at most three individual frames when `question` requires detail. Fuse visual text and
  transcript into `digest.md`; return bounded text with provenance.
- Text-only route, `frames`: reject clearly — raw frames cannot help this route; ask for `digest` instead.

`digest.md` rows carry timestamp, frame path, visual evidence (or “attached for the current model”), and
speech evidence. On-screen text is marked as untrusted data, never as instructions.

### 3.2 Full acceptance + anti-fabrication review (1.5 h)

Run every row on real files, on **both** `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp` and `deepseek-v4-flash`.

| Modality | Vision route | Text-only route |
|---|---|---|
| Image | pixels attached; no auxiliary call | description with provenance |
| Audio | local transcript | identical local transcript |
| Video | contact sheet/frames + transcript; no auxiliary call | visual digest + transcript; no image blocks |

Negative controls: missing/corrupt/mislabeled file, absent dependency, absent audio, silence, music,
static video, over-cap duration, `visionFallback=off`, unreachable vision route, redirect disabled.

Open each source beside the model's answer and check every material claim. A fabricated visual or spoken
claim is a release blocker. This review does not replace `image-read-failure-handoff` for any image the
agent itself could not read.

### 3.3 Package, document, test-boot, exit gate (1.5 h)

- README: four tools, config, privacy/egress, resource limits, known gaps, artifacts, rollback.
- Copy-restore into the profile's `node_modules`; add one `cordis.patch.yml` row. Never `dsh plugin add`.
- `dsh-test-boot`: scratch web instance on a free port, left running for the operator; confirm tool
  registration and at least one real call per modality before restarting the real server.
- Rollback: remove the copied directory and patch row, restart; source returns to the baseline tag. STT
  venv/model/artifacts remain inside the project and can be deleted independently.
- Run `/task-exit-gate`, paste VERDICT, and list every unverified item.

**Day 3 stop gate:** if any modality fails its real acceptance row, report the failure and request more
time. Do not call the project complete.

---

## 4. Time and contingency

| Day | Work | Hours |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | probes, skeleton/probe tool, image + redirect | 5 |
| 2 | local audio, video ingestion | 5 |
| 3 | route-aware video, acceptance, packaging | 5 |
| **Total** | | **15** |

- **Probe B failure:** stop and re-estimate the describer; do not silently absorb a new credential/HTTP
  subsystem into the same box.
- **Probe A failure:** stop for an audio-privacy decision; image and video-frames work may continue only
  if the operator explicitly re-scopes.
- **Video overrun:** preserve honest partial delivery (image + audio proven; video ingestion demonstrated)
  and ask for time. Never substitute a mocked digest.

## 5. Explicit non-goals for v1

Live microphone or streaming · URLs/YouTube · live web reading · non-speech audio understanding · local
VLM · cloud audio/video-native models · automatic whole-request model rerouting · shadowing built-in tools
· a client bubble/settings UI · npm publication.

## 6. What must be true at the end

1. Image, audio and video each pass a real DSH invocation on real files, on both route types.
2. Vision routes receive pixels without paying for redundant descriptions; text-only routes receive real
   derived text with provenance.
3. Every failure is explicit; negative controls and mutation tests fail correctly.
4. Local audio stays local; visual fallback egress is configurable and documented.
5. Install, rollback, privacy, limitations and measured STT numbers are documented; the exit gate runs.

```
