```
## docs/plugin-distribution-bundle.md

```
# Shipping a DSH plugin to another workstation — what the bundle must contain

Learned 2026-11-03 while packaging `dsh-media-reader` for distribution. A plugin tarball that ships only
code fails on the first colleague's machine, because the harness knowledge lives in skills, not in the
package.

## The bundle contract

```
dsh-media-reader-<version>/
  README.md            install-first, readable by a human AND an LLM (no rendering, no images)
  INSTALL.md           the exact steps for both routes, with the failure modes named
  MANIFEST.json        every file with its sha256, plus what is optional
  install.sh           copy-restore; refuses pnpm; runs the duplicate guard; prints next steps
  uninstall.sh         removes the copy and the patch row, leaves the profile otherwise untouched
  plugin/              lib/ python/ package.json cordis.patch.yml README.md
  skills/              product-motion-studio, dsh-plugin-install-safety, dsh-skill-install, dsh-test-boot
  docs/                research, pipeline, acceptance record, direction workflows, pipeline commands
  fixtures/            the small proof files the smoke test needs
  smoke.sh             runs the live capability check against a scratch instance
```

## Why each part is mandatory

| Part | Failure it prevents |
|---|---|
| `skills/dsh-plugin-install-safety` | the colleague runs `dsh plugin add`, pnpm materialises a second `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`, and **every** tool call dies with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')` |
| `skills/dsh-skill-install` | the skills are copied but never linked into `$DSH_HOME/skills`, so no slash command exists and the agent never loads them |
| `skills/dsh-test-boot` | the plugin is installed into the live profile and the server restarted blind; a boot crash costs the operator a session |
| `skills/product-motion-studio` | the plugin gives the model *eyes*; without the production skill it has no method, and produces slop that costs more than the plugin saved |
| `MANIFEST.json` | a partial copy: someone takes `lib/` and forgets `python/`, and STT silently disappears |
| `smoke.sh` | "installed" is not "working" — the check drives real sessions on both the vision and the text-only route |
| `docs/` | the next session cannot re-derive prices, limits, or why a technique was rejected, and pays for the same lesson twice |

## Rules

- **No credentials, no machine paths, no private vault references.** Placeholders in docs, literal values
  only in a git-ignored local file.
- **`README.md` must be readable as plain text** — no badges that carry meaning, no screenshots required to
  install. An LLM reading the tarball must be able to act on it.
- **Install must be reversible in one command**, and `uninstall.sh` must not touch anything it did not create.
- **Verify on a clean profile**, not the one it was developed in: copy into a throwaway `DSH_HOME`, run the
  guards, boot the scratch server, run `smoke.sh`, then tear it down.

```


---

## skills/dsh-plugin-install-safety/SKILL.md

```
---
name: dsh-plugin-install-safety
description: Prevent and diagnose the DSH crash "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')" — a split-Symbol failure caused by duplicate @deepseek-ai/dsh-* packages after plugin installs. Use before/after any `dsh plugin` install and whenever a DSH tool call (web_search, browse, etc.) fails with that error or returns no results.
---

# DSH Plugin Install Safety (split-Symbol crash)

## When this applies

- Installing, updating, or removing any DSH plugin (`dsh plugin add/remove`).
- Any DSH session where tool calls die with
  `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')` — or `web_search`
  suddenly returns "no results" after a plugin install.

## The failure (why it crashes)

DSH tool dispatch looks up the scheduler by a **module-level `Symbol`**:

```js
// @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop/lib/index.js:193
const prepared = await ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare(call.exec);
```

`TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER = Symbol("@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.scheduler")` lives in
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`. If that package is loaded from **two physical copies**,
the two `Symbol` instances are not `===`, the lookup returns `undefined`, and
`undefined.prepare(...)` throws on **every** tool call.

Two copies appear when pnpm runs inside a profile directory: the profile uses
`nodeLinker: hoisted` and plugins declare `@deepseek-ai/*` peerDependencies, so
pnpm materializes real `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` directories next to the symlinks.

## Before installing

1. Run **repo-vetting** on the plugin first (mandatory pre-install rule).
2. Pin a version compatible with the local DSH
   (e.g. local DSH 0.1.1-rc.2 → plugin `@latest`).
3. **Do NOT put pnpm on PATH for this work.** It is absent from the default PATH, and that absence is
   what makes the crash below unreachable by accident.

## Install — NEVER with `dsh plugin add` on this machine

**`dsh plugin --profile web add <pkg>` IS the crash vector. It is banned here.**

This skill previously said "install (only the official CLI)" and told you to put pnpm on PATH first.
That was wrong, and the second half *enabled* the crash. Corrected 2026-09-27 — evidence below.

Verified from the CLI source (DSH 0.1.1-rc.2):

- `lib/bin.js:96` describes the command as *"forwarding the remaining arguments to **pnpm in the
  profile directory**"*.
- `lib/plugin-9h8shc4d.js:108` — `spawnSync("pnpm", …)` with `cwd` = the profile directory.

So **"use the official CLI" and "never run pnpm inside a profile" are the same act.** A hand-written
plugin makes it worse: our own `package.json` declares `@deepseek-ai/*` as **peerDependencies** — the
exact shape that makes pnpm hoist real copies beside the profile's symlinks.

This is not theoretical: it is the failure already recorded in `concepts/dsh-browser-audit.md:222`
("why `dsh plugin add` is banned on this machine") and twice in the journals.

### The safe method — copy real files, register in the patch layer

The method `dsh-cost-bubble` has used since 2026-09-02: it has survived server restarts and a whole
harness reinstall, because no package manager is ever in the loop.

```bash
DEST="$HOME/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules/<pkg-name>"
mkdir -p "$DEST"
cp -r <src>/lib <src>/package.json "$DEST"/
```

```yaml
# ~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml  (append)
- insert:
    - id: <id>
      name: '<pkg-name>'
```

Bare `@deepseek-ai/*` imports then resolve through `~/.dsh/profiles/node_modules/` — the shared tree
of symlinks into the ONE global copy — so no dependency needs installing at all.

## After every install — verify no duplicate

```bash
find ~/.dsh/profiles -type d -path '*/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/*'
```

- **Empty output = healthy** — the profile's `@deepseek-ai/*` entries are symlinks
  to the single global copy.
- **Any output = a materialized duplicate** — the next tool call will split the
  Symbol and crash.

## If a duplicate appears (or the crash already happened)

1. Remove the materialized copy so resolution falls back to the single global copy:
   ```bash
   rm -rf ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/<pkg>
   # or the whole scope dir if unsure:
   rm -rf ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/@deepseek-ai
   ```
2. Restart the server: `dsh web`.
3. Re-run the `find` above until it prints nothing.

## Diagnosing the crash

- Symptom: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')`
  on a tool call; `web_search` may just return "no results" instead of erroring.
- Confirm exactly one physical copy on disk:
  ```bash
  find ~/.dsh ~/.nvm/versions/node/*/lib/node_modules -type d -name dsh-tools \
    | xargs realpath | sort -u
  ```
  **Group the result by node installation before reading it.** This check counts copies across
  *node versions*, and a duplicate there is **not** a split Symbol. What splits a process's Symbol
  is two copies inside **one process's resolution path**. Corrected 2026-10-02, after this check
  printed two paths (`v22.23.2`, `v24.20.0`) on a perfectly healthy machine. Ask the decisive
  question instead:

  ```bash
  # where do bare @deepseek-ai/* imports actually resolve from a plugin?
  ls -l ~/.dsh/profiles/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/ | awk '{print $11}' | sort -u
  node -e 'console.log(require.resolve("@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools",{paths:[process.env.HOME+"/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules"]}))'
  ```

  Every line must land in **one** node installation — the one `/usr/local/bin/dsh` runs. On
  2026-10-02 they all pointed at `v24.20.0` while the `v22.23.2` tree was an unreachable leftover
  of an older node. Guard 3 (duplicates under `profiles/*/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/`) was empty,
  and **that** is the real vector. The blunt "must print one path" reading would have aborted a
  correct install.

## Verified against source (DSH 0.1.1-rc.2)

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools/lib/index.js:2416` — `const TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER = Symbol("@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.scheduler")`
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools/lib/index.js:2564` — `ToolRuntime[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER] = { prepare, dispatch, finalize, finish }`
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop/lib/index.js:193` — `ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare(call.exec)`

Subtle variant to watch for: `dsh-tools` ships a **dual build** — main
`lib/index.js` and subpath `lib/types/*.js` each define their own Symbol. A plugin
importing `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools/types` (or `./presentation`) directly while the
core uses the main entry also splits the Symbol, even with no duplicate on disk.

## Related

- Vault learning: `learnings/dsh-tool-prepare-split-symbol.md`
- Vault concept: `concepts/dsh-plugin-ecosystem.md`
- `repo-vetting` skill — run it before every install.

## Where to install on this machine (2026-09-27)

The method above is unchanged wherever you install. What differs is **which home**:

| target | when |
|---|---|
| `~/dsh-planner` — the durable planner home, instance **3099** | the default for this machine: it survives a reboot, and it is where the planner and cost-bubble are installed and tested |
| `~/.dsh` — the operator's real home, instance **3080** | **only when the operator asks for it.** Installing means restarting 3080, which ends their live session; and their planner data does NOT follow the plugin (the register lives in `~/dsh-planner/storages/`), so the store must be moved in the same change. The checklist is in [[planner-config-fields-plan]] |

`scripts/deploy.sh` in the planner repo does the copy half and **refuses outright** for any target under
`~/.dsh`, because `DSH_HOME` is set in every process the harness spawns — including an agent session —
so a default that reads it silently points at the live profile. It also runs the guard below after
copying.

```


---

## skills/dsh-skill-install/SKILL.md

```
---
name: dsh-skill-install
description: Make a skill invocable as a "/name" slash command in the DSH Web composer, and in any DSH profile, by linking it into $DSH_HOME/skills — then verify it actually loads. Use when the user wants a slash command for a skill, when a skill does not show up in the DSH composer, when adding a brand-new skill, or when a skill works in Claude Code but not in DSH.
---

# DSH Skill Install (make a skill slash-invocable)

Turn any `SKILL.md` into a **user-global DSH skill**, so typing `/<name>` in the DSH Web
composer loads it — in every DSH profile (`web`, `headless`, `tui`, …) and every project.

## Why this exists (the one fact that matters)

**DSH reads `$DSH_HOME/skills`, not `~/.claude/skills`.** The vault installs skills into
`~/.claude/skills/`, `~/.kimi-code/skills/`, and project `.claude/skills/` — none of which
`dsh-skill-filesystem` looks at. So a vault skill can be perfectly healthy everywhere else and
simply not exist as far as DSH is concerned. That is the whole bug this skill fixes.

## Where DSH looks

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem` merges these roots (`includeDefaultRoots` defaults true):

| root | source | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `<projectRoot>/.dsh/skills` | `project-dsh` | nearest project root of the session cwd |
| `<projectRoot>/.agents/skills` | `project-agents` | |
| configured `customSkillDirs` | `custom` | per-profile plugin config |
| **`$DSH_HOME/skills`** (`~/.dsh/skills`) | `user-dsh` | **the global user root — install here** |
| `$DSH_AGENTS_HOME/skills` (`~/.agents/skills`) | `user-agents` | |
| bundled | `bundled` | ships with the harness |

## File format contract

- Layout is either `<root>/<name>/SKILL.md` (**directory bundle**) or `<root>/<name>.md` (**flat**).
  Use the directory bundle: its `resourceBase` resolves to the skill's own folder.
- Frontmatter is **mandatory** and must supply non-empty `name` **and** `description`, or the file
  is silently skipped with `skill file … ignored: frontmatter requires name and description`.
- `name` must match `/^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/` (kebab-case, no underscores, no capitals).
- A root entry that is neither a directory nor a `.md` file is ignored — but a stray `README.md`
  **is** parsed and warns. Keep non-skills out of the root.

## Invocation policy (and the trap that silently kills a skill)

Canonical frontmatter keys are **`disable-model-invocation`** and **`user-invocable`**.

> **Trap:** the camelCase keys `userInvocable`, `modelInvocable`, and `disableModelInvocation`
> **throw at parse time** and the file is **discarded**. A Claude-Code-style `userInvocable: true`
> line silently removes the skill from DSH. Never add it.

Defaults: `modelInvocable: true`, `userInvocable: true`. **So a normal skill needs no invocation
frontmatter at all to be slash-invocable** — just `name` + `description`.

## Procedure

Preferred — the vault installer (idempotent, audits every link, accepts any source dir):

```bash
V=$VAULT
"$V/scripts/install-dsh-skills.sh"                 # default source: the vault skills dir
"$V/scripts/install-dsh-skills.sh" /some/other/dir # any dir of *-SKILL.md or */SKILL.md
```

Inline equivalent, when the script is unavailable:

```bash
SRC=/path/to/skills            # files named <name>-SKILL.md  or  <name>/SKILL.md
ROOT="${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills"
mkdir -p "$ROOT"
for f in "$SRC"/*-SKILL.md; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || continue
  name=$(sed -n 's/^name:[[:space:]]*//p' "$f" | head -1 | tr -d '\r')
  [ -n "$name" ] || { echo "no name in $f" >&2; continue; }
  mkdir -p "$ROOT/$name"
  ln -sfn "$f" "$ROOT/$name/SKILL.md"
  echo "linked $name"
done
```

Always **link, never copy** — the canonical file stays the single source of truth, and editing it
propagates to every target (see [[mistake-guardrails-SKILL]]).

## Verify — two independent checks

**1. Real registry (authoritative).** Drive the actual skill service; do not eyeball the directory.

```js
const BASE = '$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.20.0/lib/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai'
const { Context } = await import(`${BASE}/cordis/lib/index.js`)
const skill = await import(`${BASE}/dsh-skill/lib/index.js`)
const fsProvider = await import(`${BASE}/dsh-skill-filesystem/lib/index.js`)

const ctx = new Context()
ctx.plugin(skill.default)
ctx.plugin(fsProvider, { dshHome: process.env.HOME + '/.dsh', agentsHome: process.env.HOME + '/.agents' })

// GOTCHA: ctx.skills is undefined until the service registers asynchronously.
for (let i = 0; i < 60 && ctx.skills === undefined; i++) await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 100))

const list = await ctx.skills.list({ cwd: process.cwd() })   // bound this with a timeout
const s = list.find(x => x.name === 'my-skill')
console.log(s, skill.isUserInvocable(s))   // isUserInvocable gates the human-facing /slash catalog
```

**2. Live effect.** The running DSH instance re-advertises the catalog on its own — after linking,
the skills show up in an **already-open session**. If a fresh link is missing only in the browser,
that is a tab refresh, not a failure.

## Hot reload: no restart needed

`watch` and `watchFollowSymlinks` both default to **true**, so added/edited skills are picked up
live (observed directly). **Skill installs therefore do not need a server restart**, which means
[[dsh-test-boot-SKILL]] does **not** apply here — that rule is for plugin and
`cordis.patch.yml` changes that only take effect on restart. Only the browser tab may need a
refresh for the slash menu.

## Vault policy: install to every target

Per the standing rule in `skills/README.md`, a skill is global by default. The full target list
(all symlinks to the one canonical vault file):

```bash
V=$VAULT
install_to() {  # quoted args only — never a space-separated for-list
  local name="$1"; shift
  for t in "$@"; do
    mkdir -p "$t/$name"
    ln -sfn "$V/skills/$name-SKILL.md" "$t/$name/SKILL.md"
  done
}
install_to my-skill \
  "$HOME/.claude/skills" "$HOME/.kimi-code/skills" "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills" \
  $HOME/projects/China-to-Kenya-Import-App/.claude/skills \
  $HOME/projects/digital-front-desk/.claude/skills \
  $HOME/projects/flywheel-control-centre/.claude/skills \
  "$HOME/projects/Marketing/.claude/skills" \
  "$HOME/projects/Quick Cash/.claude/skills" \
  $HOME/credit/credit_payments/.claude/skills
```

Note the quoting: `Marketing` is fine, but **`Quick Cash` has a space** and must be quoted — the
exact mistake logged in [[mistake-guardrails-SKILL]].

## The trap that cost a skill its whole life: PRESENT IS NOT PARSEABLE

Every check in `install-dsh-skills.sh` used to be `sed`/`grep` against lines, and the audit reported
`installed: 22 | skipped: 0 | broken: 0 | mismatches: 0` while **`field-request` had never once
loaded**. Its frontmatter had `name:` and `description:` — and was **invalid YAML**, because the
description was a plain scalar containing an unquoted `": "`:

```yaml
description: Guide the operator ... instead of a question: the priority subset first, ...
```

DSH parses frontmatter as YAML. That line is a hard parse error, the file is discarded in silence, and
no line-based check can see it.

**Therefore: always parse the frontmatter, never grep it.** The installer now calls
`scripts/skill_frontmatter_problem.py` on every source and every installed link, and reports
`unloadable: N`.

**Quote any description containing `": "`** — single quotes are safest, and keep it on ONE line so a
line-based reader also gets it whole.

### And a guard that could not fail

The first version of that check resolved its helper as `"$VAULT/scripts/…"` — but `$VAULT` is the
**skills directory**, not the vault root, so the path did not exist. With `2>/dev/null`, the failure
was **swallowed and read as "no problem found"**. Reintroducing the broken frontmatter did not trip
it: it printed `unloadable: 0` on a skill it could never open.

Two rules follow, and they are the same rule twice:

- **Resolve a helper from the script's own directory** (`SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"`), never from a variable that means something else.
- **A checker that cannot RUN must report UNVERIFIED, not clean.** The installer now counts
  `unverified:` separately, so silence is never mistaken for a pass. See [[a-guard-that-cannot-fail]]
  and [[the-check-must-prove-it-ran]].

## Traps

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| Skill works in Claude Code, absent in DSH | It is only in `~/.claude/skills`; DSH never reads it |
| `skill file … ignored: frontmatter requires name and description` | Missing/empty `name` or `description` |
| Linked, resolving, both keys present — **and not in the registry** | Frontmatter is **invalid YAML** (an unquoted `": "` in `description` is the usual cause). `sed` finds the keys; the parser rejects the block. Real case: `field-request`, never loaded. |
| `ignored: invalid skill name` | Not kebab-case (underscores, capitals, leading digit) |
| `ignored: invalid invocation frontmatter` | Legacy camelCase key — use `user-invocable` |
| `ignored: missing YAML frontmatter` | No `---` block on line 1 (a stray `README.md` in the root) |
| In the model catalog but not in the slash menu | `user-invocable: false` is set |
| Link points at nothing | Canonical file moved/renamed; re-run the installer and read its audit |

## Related

- [[dsh-global-skill-root]] — the verified facts behind every claim here
- [[repo-vetting-SKILL]] · [[dsh-plugin-install-safety-SKILL]] · [[dsh-test-boot-SKILL]]
- [[mistake-guardrails-SKILL]] — symlink-to-canonical and quoting rules

